title: 116 YA KUN KAYA TOAST EATEN?! | Eating 58 SERVINGS OF YA KUN KAYA TOASTS FOR SINGAPORE NATIONAL DAY!
description:
In this video, we're celebrating Singapore's National Day at the Ya Kun and we've decided to do a special food challenge to commemorate Singapore's 58th Birthday. I've always wanted to do food challenges for National Day and can't think of a better idea than to eat 58 servings (116 pieces) of Ya Kun Kaya Toast - which symbolized the nation's 58th birthday. It wasn’t the easiest challenge, but I still enjoyed it! 

Ya Kun Kaya Toast is one of Singapore's representative foods due to its iconic status and popularity among locals and tourists alike. Each serving consists of toasted bread slices spread with kaya, a sweet coconut and egg jam, and served with a generous slab of butter. It is usually accompanied by soft-boiled eggs and a cup of kopi or teh. 

Last but not least, I would like to wish Singapore a Happy 58th National Day!

title: The Secret recipe of making perfect Kaya Toast better than Ya Kun Singapore
description:
Are you ready to unlock the secrets of making the most delicious kaya toast?  In this video, we'll guide you through the entire process, from creating your very own homemade kaya jam to assembling the perfect kaya toast sandwich that rivals Ya Kun or ToastBox.

What is kaya jam? It's a rich, creamy coconut and egg custard with a hint of pandan flavour - a true taste of Southeast Asia! We'll show you traditional techniques for making authentic kaya jam that will leave you craving more.

But kaya jam isn't just for toast! Get creative with these ideas:

Drizzle it over pancakes or waffles
Swirl it into your morning porridge
Use it as a filling for sweet buns or pastries
Love our kaya jam? You're in luck! We proudly offer our homemade kaya for sale on our website (https://mei-mei-london.myshopify.com/collections/pantry)  Order yours today and experience the taste of tradition (UK DELIVERIES ONLY)

4-5 eggs - good quality
200g caster sugar
375ml coconut cream
pandan leaves

For the caramel:
100g caster sugar

salt to season

title: 別再只吃亞坤了!! 新加坡海南人百年KOPITIAM 炭火現烤麵包半熟蛋才是道地| 新加坡自由行EP20
description:
這支影片帶您造訪號稱新加坡第一家、歷史最悠久的海南人咖啡店——Killiney Kopitiam（舊名瓊和興）。不同於現代連鎖店，這家店至今仍堅持以火炭烘烤麵包，呈現傳統的碳香味，搭配招牌咖椰醬和完美的半熟蛋，被我認證為「比雅坤更好吃」的道地風味。

影片中特別點了新馬傳統早餐套裝，並深入探討了咖椰醬（Kaya）的文化意義，以及海南人如何在早期南洋謀生，將歐洲的咖啡、麵包與馬來、華人飲食文化融合，最終創造出獨特的新馬 Kopitiam 文化。

最令人驚喜的是，這裡的咖哩雞塊搭配麵包獲得我極高評價，咖哩醬汁濃郁，雞肉大塊入味 
如果您到新加坡旅遊，想品嚐最正宗、最棒的平民美食早餐，Killiney Kopitiam 絕對是不能錯過的選擇。影片最後也詳細介紹了新馬咖啡店的點餐術語，如 Kopi、Kopi O、Kopi C 等的區別。強烈推薦給所有熱愛新馬美食文化的朋友！

Killiney Kopitiam 
67 Killiney Rd, Singapore 239525

[05:39] 深入解析**「咖椰」（Kaya）**的由來（馬來文意為「有錢人」）。
[06:14] 文化探討：新馬傳統早餐如何融合馬來、歐洲與華人文化。

[14:27] 總結評論：Killiney Kopitiam 食物穩定、味道超乎預期。
[14:55] 強烈推薦 Killiney Kopitiam 為新加坡旅遊必吃早餐店。

A century-old Singapore Hainanese KOPITIAM — charcoal-toasted bread and half-boiled eggs are the authentic way | Singapore independent travel EP20 || This video visits Killiney Kopitiam (formerly Qiong He Xing), billed as Singapore's first and oldest Hainanese coffee shop. Unlike modern chains, it still toasts bread over charcoal for a traditional smoky aroma; with its signature kaya and perfect half-boiled eggs, I certify it as authentic flavour 'better than Ya Kun'. I ordered the traditional Singapore-Malaysia breakfast set and explored kaya's cultural meaning and how early Hainanese in Nanyang fused European coffee and bread with Malay and Chinese food cultures, creating the unique Singapore-Malaysia kopitiam culture. The curry chicken with bread was a highlight. If you visit Singapore and want the most authentic, best everyday breakfast, Killiney Kopitiam is a must. The video ends with kopitiam ordering terms like Kopi, Kopi O, Kopi C.

title: Singapore’s MOST ICONIC Breakfast |  Iconic Foods In Singapore Ep.3 | Ya Kun Kaya Toast
description:
In Episode 3 of Iconic Foods in Singapore, I explore one of the most famous and nostalgic breakfasts in the country — Ya Kun Kaya Toast.

Ya Kun Kaya Toast is a true Singapore institution that has been around for decades, serving what many locals consider the most iconic Singaporean breakfast. From office workers to tourists, this simple yet legendary meal is deeply rooted in Singapore’s food culture.

During my visit, I tried the Signature Kaya Toast Set ($6.30) which includes:
• Crispy toasted bread with kaya & butter
• Two soft-boiled eggs seasoned with soy sauce & pepper
• A cup of traditional Singapore-style kopi

This classic combo perfectly represents Singapore’s kopi culture and heritage breakfast — simple, affordable, and incredibly comforting.

If you’re visiting Singapore, this is one breakfast you MUST try. Whether it’s your first time or you grew up eating this, Ya Kun Kaya Toast remains timeless.

Ya Kun Kaya Toast is available islandwide across Singapore, so google the location to find one nearest to you.

If you enjoy videos on Singapore food, iconic local dishes, and heritage eats, don’t forget to like, comment, and subscribe for more episodes of Iconic Foods in Singapore.

title: Singapore Kaya Toast Review - Ya Kun Kaya Toast VS Killiney Kopitiam Kaya Toast
description:
Singapore Kaya Toast Review - Ya Kun Kaya Toast VS Killiney Kopitiam Kaya Toast

My name is Joel Liu and I am the National Food Bro the Singapore food reviewer! 

My quest to find the best Singapore Kaya Toast in Singapore has led me to 2 iconic Kaya Toast Kopitiam! There are numerous famous Kaya Toast brands in Singapore such as Ah Kong Den Kaya Toast, Kopi Alley Kaya Toast, Chin Mee Chin Kaya Toast, Heap Seng Leong Kaya Toast, Keng Wah Sung Kaya Toast, Toast Box Kaya Toast and Funbox Kaya Toast just to name a few. But where can we find the best Kaya Toast in Singapore? Today our Kaya Toast contestants today are:

Yakun Kaya Toast
from
Paya Lebar Square
60 Paya Lebar # 01-87
Singapore 409051

AND

Killiney Kopitiam Kaya Toast
from
Katong Square
88 East Coast Road # 01-11 
Singapore 423371

So what is Kaya Toast? Kaya toast is a traditional Singapore breakfast item from the early 1900s.  It is famous Singaporean snack and in Malaysia as well. It can also be served as an afternoon snack usually to kids. This dish was invented by Hainan immigrants to the Malay peninsula. Malaysians and Singaporeans often east Kaya Toast with a cup of hot beverage such as Teh C, Kopi C, Teh O, Kopi O or even Milo peng. This merits the snack's inclusion in many Singapore Kopitiams. Singaporean companies such as Yakun Kaya Toast and Killiney Kopitiam are franchises serve the most popular Singapore kaya toast.

Most people are familiar with breakfast toast. But what is this "Kaya" that is the highlight of this Singaporean breakfast? Kaya is simply coconut jam. Kaya is traditionally made from a topping of sugar, coconut milk, Pandan Leaf and eggs. Kaya is generally served on toast, and also sometimes on crackers. Kaya is spread generously onto 2 slices of toasted bread but that is not all, thick slices of butter cut from SCS Pure Creamery Butter Block will be placed on the spread toast to complete this sandwich. Just like how you cannot eat Hamburgers without a serving of french fries, Kaya Toast is always served with 2 soft boiled eggs. After seasoning the soft-boiled eggs with a little dark soy sauce and white pepper, these eggs also serve as a dipping sauce for the Kaya Toast!

title: KAYA TOAST : EST. 1944 YA KUN Coffee and Toast stall | A Singaporean Living Tradition
description:
YA KUN KAYA TOAST:

Kaya Toast is a dish consisting of two slices of toast with butter  and
kaya (coconut jam), commonly served alongside coffee and 
soft boiled eggs. In Singapore, the dish is commonly consumed for breakfast . It became integrated into Kopi Tiam (coffee shop) culture, being widely available in food chains such as YA KUN KAYA TOAST.  

Ya Kun started in 1944 as a Coffee stall selling Kaya Toast, Soft boiled eggs and Coffee in Telok Ayer Basin. Being world famous for its signature crispy kaya toast and nostalgic coffee, this Singaporean brand with a history of more than 78 years has won the hearts of many around the World.

Ya Kun Kaya Toast is slice of bread into half and combining the toast with homemade Kaya, this became their signature Kaya Toast. 

Registered in 1944 as Ya Kun Coffee stall (Ya Kun being Ah Koon in Hanyu Pinyin), the stall gradually developed a reputation for delicious Kaya Toast and friendly service. The couple, their eight children and seven other families lived together in a three-storey shophouse across the road, where the Hong Leong Building now stands. As the children grew up, they began to help stir the Kaya, run errands, charcoal-grill the bread and eventually, manage the stall.

title: Ya Kun 亚坤品牌发展史：从传统咖啡摊到国际品牌
description:
你每天熟悉的新加坡国民早餐——咖椰吐司与咖啡，背后究竟有着怎样的创业故事？

本集带你认识 Ya Kun 亚坤，从早期咖啡摊的发展开始，了解创办人黎亚坤（Loi Ah Koon）的南洋历程、招牌咖椰的诞生，以及这个传统品牌如何经历关键转折，逐步走向国际市场。

一家熟悉的咖啡店，如何从早期的小生意发展成为具有代表性的品牌？让我们透过历史资料，一起寻找答案。

📚 **本集内容｜六个章节**

**第一章：熟悉的国民早餐**
认识 Ya Kun 亚坤，以及咖椰吐司和咖啡如何成为许多人熟悉的新加坡早餐组合。

**第二章：黎亚坤的南洋历程**
从海南来到新加坡的年轻移民，如何开始自己的谋生之路，并踏入咖啡摊的行业？

**第三章：招牌咖椰的诞生**
认识亚坤招牌咖椰与吐司背后的故事，了解传统食品如何逐渐成为品牌特色。

**第四章：1998 年的关键转折**
回顾亚坤迁至 Far East Square 的重要阶段，以及家族经营与品牌发展的变化。

**第五章：国际特许经营之路**
从传统咖啡摊到特许经营，了解亚坤如何探索新的经营模式，并逐步走向海外市场。

**第六章：亚坤的历史遗产**
一段创业历史如何延续至今？从传统饮食、家族传承到品牌文化，认识亚坤留下的商业与文化印记。

title: Half Boiled Eggs and Toast | Singapore Recipes | Recipes Are Simple
description:
Half Boiled Eggs -  Breakfast Loved by an entire Nation!

A typical Singapore-style breakfast at a KOPITIAM (coffee shop) often consists of soft-boiled eggs, along with kaya toast and a cup of kopi (coffee) or teh(tea).

Singapore-style soft-boiled eggs differ from soft-boiled eggs in the West. Our soft-boiled eggs are runny and wobbly, and you crack them open like you would a raw egg, whereas in the West, the white is more firmly cooked - the egg, peeled like a hard-boiled egg or top taken off - and the yolk, is runny.

Let's learn how to make the Singapore Half Boiled Eggs at home, with perfect results!
From my blog: https://www.recipesaresimple.com/half-boiled-eggs-favorite-singapore-breakfast/

description:
Think of this as a traditional muslin bag except it is made of woven 100% cotton instead of muslin.

The cloth is sewn onto a plastic ring with a handle, making it a bag instead of just a flat piece of cloth.

When you add contents to be strained, the weight will not cause the free floating cloth to sink.

You can also suspend the bag over a bowl to keep your hands free as you pour.

This bag is traditionally used for making coffee. Put your coffee grounds inside the bag and pour hot water over it to use it like a drip filter.

The bag can also be used for to make homemade soy milk. After blending the soybeans with water, pour the mixture into the bag in small batches and squeeze the bag to get milk. You can also make other natural milks in this manner.

Hand wash with hot water after using. Hang to air dry.

title: Kaya Toast & Eggs 🥚
description:
Kaya Toast and Eggs:

Serves: 4
Prep time:  10 mins
Cook time: 25 mins

Ingredients
Kaya Jam
1 cup (250ml) coconut cream
4 egg yolks, lightly beaten
2 tbsp (40g) caster sugar
60g palm sugar, chopped
4 pandan leaves
¼ tsp sea salt
Kaya Toast
8 eggs, at room temperature
Soy sauce, to season
White pepper, to season
8 thick slices soft white bread
150g butter, cold, sliced
Method
For the Kaya jam, heat coconut milk in a heat proof bowl over a saucepan of simmering water with the sugars, pandan leaves and salt. Stir constantly, until mixture almost boils, then remove from heat. 
Place the egg yolks in a medium bowl. Whisk a ladleful of milk mixture gradually into eggs, then transfer back to the bowl over the saucepan and place back on the heat. 
Stir constantly for 10-15 minutes, until mixture thickens and has the texture of custard. 
Remove pandan leaves and pour Kaya into a sterilised jar and it will thicken further on cooling*. 
For the eggs, bring a large pot of water to the boil. Gently add the eggs then remove from the heat immediately. 
Leave eggs for 4 minutes**, then plunge into iced water. 
Toast bread over an open flame or on a grill until lightly charred. Sandwich slices together with a generous spread of Kaya jam and slices of butter. 
Cut off the crusts, then slice into 3 fingers.  
Remove eggs from the water and carefully break into individual serving dishes. Season with a dash of soy and white pepper. 
Serve eggs with Kaya toast and a fresh coffee. 
*Store refrigerated for up to 1 week. 
**Eggs will need a minute longer if they are cooked from cold.

description:
Welcome to Singapore! 

For Part 2 of our Singapore Travel Vlog in collaboration with  @VisitSingapore   we take a bite out of the very best of Singaporean Street Food. This city's cuisine is as vibrant and diverse as its inhabitants, and we are so lucky to try everything from a traditional Singaporean breakfast (with kaya toast, of course) to a bustling Zi Char feast to a stylish Raffles Hotel creperie to the modern Malay flavors of Kampong Glam. The best Chili crab, satay sticks, horfun, teh tarik and even a french omelette round out our amazing 4 day itinerary of the lion city.

title: What’s Open at Maxwell Food Centre in the Morning? | Iconic Singapore Breakfast at 8AM!
description:
We started our day with a peaceful morning walk from Teck Lim Road to Maxwell Food Centre in Chinatown, Singapore — just a quick 5-minute stroll from Butternut Tree Hotel.

At 8AM, the streets were calm, some stalls were just opening, and we got lucky with no line at Tian Tian Hainanese Chicken Rice! We also grabbed a traditional kaya toast set with soft-boiled egg from 1950’s Coffee — perfect Singapore breakfast combo.

If you're planning a food trip to Chinatown, this video shows why visiting Maxwell Food Centre in the morning is a smart move.

🍽️ Must-Try Stalls at Maxwell Food Centre:
Tian Tian Hainanese Chicken Rice – World-famous chicken rice with tender meat and fragrant rice
Ah Tai Chicken Rice – Great alternative with shorter lines
1950’s Coffee – Traditional kaya toast, kopi, and soft-boiled eggs
Fuzhou Oyster Cake – Crispy, savory fritters packed with minced meat and oysters
China Street Fritters – Classic ngoh hiang and handmade Teochew snacks
Zhen Zhen Porridge – Comforting Cantonese-style porridge (arrive early!)
Hainanese Curry Rice – Messy but delicious mix of curry, pork chop, and sides
Hum Jin Pang – DIY fried dough sticks with sweet or savory filling
Danlao – Silky scrambled egg rice bowls, simple and satisfying
Jin Hua Fish Bee Hoon – Light and comforting fish soup noodles
Fu Shun Roast Meats & Noodles – Roast pork, char siew, and duck with springy noodles
Hajmeer Kwaja – Indian-Muslim stall serving mee goreng and flavorful briyani

Sprinkle some pepper and soy sauce on those eggs, and decide between a cup of joe or a comforting tea. Trust me, it's a breakfast adventure worth having when you are in Singapore! MUST !

title: Traditional Singapore breakfast by Shen Suarez
description:
Rise and Shine! Let’s have some Traditional Singapore breakfast in Dong Po Colonial Cafe and experience the country’s coffee culture. 

Sip a cup of Kopi ➡️  Coffee with Condensed Milk: ("Kopi" in Malay language means "Coffee")

Eat Soft Boiled Eggs with a bit of soya sauce and pepper ➡️ A typical Singapore-style breakfast at a coffee shop often consists of soft-boiled eggs.

Munch on a Kaya Toast ▶️ toasted bread filled with butter and kaya, a jam made from eggs, sugar, coconut milk and pandan leaves.

For something different try Bostock ▶️ a nutty and wonderful toast topped with almond flakes. 

A bite of something old school with Long Cup Butter Cake ➡️ is definitely meant for dip in the coffee. 

#GoodMorning
